features: THE RECORDED TOTAL IS THE ONE WRITTEN ON THE INVOICE — An electronic invoice declares its own VAT in the DatiRiepilogo blocks, one for each rate/nature pair. The program ignored that figure and recomputed it line by line, rounding each line separately: on a gas bill among the eleven used for testing, the supplier declares € 100.15 and € 100.14 was recorded. It is the difference between «round then sum» and «sum then round», and the second is what electronic invoicing prescribes. The declared tax is now distributed across the lines of its group, and the recorded total matches the document on all eleven real files, across four paths: registration, editing, reversal and prior-year debt.

IF THE ENTRY IS NOT WORTH WHAT THE DOCUMENT ASKS, YOU ARE NOW TOLD — On a received invoice the total is not ours: the debt to the supplier is what the document asks, in full. Deleting or editing a line after import updated the on-screen totals consistently with themselves and said nothing about the document being recorded. A warning now appears with both figures — «The document asks € 100.15, this entry is worth € 55.80» — and explains the consequence. It warns and does not block: the administrator remains the authority on their own document.

THE DECLARED VAT HOLDS AS LONG AS IT DESCRIBES THE LINES IN FRONT OF IT — «Taxable 45.74, tax 10.06» is a single sentence. A group's declared tax stays in force as long as that group's lines add up to the taxable amount the group declares; as soon as they diverge, that group — and only that one — falls back to line-by-line calculation. Splitting an expense across two chapters changes nothing because the sum stays the same; correcting an amount does.

REOPENING A CREDIT NOTE NO LONGER INFLATES IT — If the reversed invoice contained a reducing line, the credit note carries that line as positive. Reopening it to correct a date pushed it from −€ 100.15 to −€ 104.54: € 4.39 of credit towards the supplier matching no money at all, without a single on-screen field changing.

A REVERSAL'S CREDIT NOTE NO LONGER LOSES THE DOCUMENT'S VAT — The first save was correct, but the note did not keep the summaries of the invoice it cancels: reopening and saving it was enough for the VAT to revert to line-by-line calculation and diverge by one cent from the invoice, leaving a residue towards the supplier that nobody closes.

CLEARING THE PRIOR-YEAR DEBT RATE NO LONGER SAVES 22% SILENTLY — The screen showed zero VAT and the save applied 22%: on € 1,000.00 that is € 220.00 of debt nobody typed and that the preview had denied a moment earlier. The field is now required, because neither 22 nor 0 is what the administrator said.

AN ORDINARY INVOICE IN CREDIT CAN NOW BE REVERSED — When line reductions exceed the charges the document is worth less than zero while still being an invoice. Reversal refused it saying «you cannot reverse a credit note», which was also the wrong document type: that document was left with no way to be corrected, because editing points to reversal and reversal refused.

TWO SUMMARY BLOCKS ON THE SAME RATE NOW ADD UP — They overwrote each other, and only the last survived. The two parts of the program that answer the same question contradicted each other: on the same document the file list would show € 183.00 and the registration € 161.00.

THE LINE TOTAL SHOWN IS THE ONE THAT REACHES THE BOOKS — When the document's tax is distributed, a compensating cent can land on any line of the group: the form showed € 8.45 on a line that, once recorded, is worth € 8.46. The same figure also fed the expense charged to the chapter and the budget-overrun threshold, both short by that cent.

BACKUP TESTS NO LONGER INTERFERE BETWEEN PROJECT COPIES — The temporary databases had fixed names: running the tests in two copies of the project at once made one drop the other's databases, with failures matching no real defect.
